text:

title: Manual Snapshot - OpenToonz 1.7.1
creator: OpenToonz Explorer
text:
!! Reference baseline
The attached PDF identifies itself as ''OpenToonz Documentation, Release 1.7.1'', dated June 28, 2023. It contains 557 PDF pages and 551 numbered manual pages.

The official `/en/latest/` site also identifies the published documentation as version 1.7.1 at the time this reference package was prepared. The manual describes itself as an ongoing project, so a current OpenToonz build may differ from a documented instruction.

!! Journal rule
For every formal experiment, record the exact OpenToonz version or commit. Treat a mismatch as evidence to investigate: the application may have changed, the documentation may be stale, or the test conditions may differ.

title: Interface Overview
creator: OpenToonz Explorer
caption: Introduces rooms, dockable panes and the appearance settings that shape an OpenToonz workspace.
text:
''Manual reference'' · Chapter 5 · OpenToonz Documentation 1.7.1 · pp. 35-60
Introduces rooms, dockable panes and the appearance settings that shape an OpenToonz workspace. !! Production relevance Rooms are views of the current scene rather than separate documents. Record room purpose and layout when a test depends on a specific combination of Viewer, Xsheet, Level Strip, Palette or editor panes. !! title: Managing Projects
creator: OpenToonz Explorer
caption: Explains project roots, project definitions, default folder aliases and the Project Browser used to organize production material consistently.
text:
''Manual reference'' · Chapter 6 · OpenToonz Documentation 1.7.1 · pp. 61-74
Explains project roots, project definitions, default folder aliases and the Project Browser used to organize production material consistently. !! Production relevance Project-relative paths make a journal portable. Record intentional folder changes because moving an alias after scenes exist can break asset retrieval. !! title: Setting Up a Scene
creator: OpenToonz Explorer
caption: Collects the scene-level choices that establish units, frame rate, camera output, color calibration, Undo capacity and memory behavior.
text:

Collects the scene-level choices that establish units, frame rate, camera output, color calibration, Undo capacity and memory behavior. !! creator: OpenToonz Explorer

text:
''Manual reference'' · Chapter 10 · OpenToonz Documentation 1.7.1 · pp. 111-152
Explains direct drawing in Toonz Vector, Toonz Raster and ordinary Raster levels, along with canvas changes, drawing edits, animation techniques, onion skin and Shift and Trace. !! Production relevance Level type is a first-class test condition. The same tool name can operate on different data models, so record the level type and tool options before describing a drawing result. !! title: Using Onion Skin
tags: Reference [[OpenToonz Manual Reference]] [[Drawing Animation Levels]] [[OTPJ Online Reference]]
creator: OpenToonz Explorer
caption: Relative and fixed onion-skin markers in level and scene context.
text:
''Manual subsection reference'' · Section 10.5 · OpenToonz Documentation 1.7.1 · print pp. 149-150
Onion skin displays selected drawings before or after the current drawing as visual guides. Relative markers move with the current frame; fixed markers continue to reference chosen frames. Context also matters: Level Strip use follows the level's drawing sequence, while Xsheet or Timeline use reflects scene exposure and transformations. !! Production relevance An onion-skin report should identify relative or fixed markers, Level Strip or Xsheet/Timeline context, level-only or scene-wide display, and relevant visualization preferences such as paper thickness or lines-only display. !! Journal entries in this area <$list filter="[tagtag[Journal]sort[sequence]]" emptyMessage="''No journal entry is tagged with this manual area yet.''"> * <$link><$view field="title"/> - <$view field="status"/> !! Suggested experiment Draw four poses, compare relative and fixed markers from both the Level Strip and Xsheet, then repeat with a transformed column and record the expected coordinate space. !!
